items.title: Phasmophobia announces the jump to Unity 6 and other new features
items.summary: Kinetic Games has just revealed several new features to come to Phasmophobia. The studio is planning several major changes, including an engine upgrade.…
items.content:
Kinetic Games has just revealed several new features to come to Phasmophobia . The studio is planning several major changes, including an engine upgrade.

As a result, the cooperative psychological horror game will soon be upgraded to Unity 6, delivering improved performance and more realistic lighting. Additionally, the game will be compatible with Xbox Play Anywhere, and the modeling of player-controlled characters is expected to see significant improvements as well. During an investigation, players will be able to use a new item: divining rods. This will prove particularly useful on large maps to help locate the area occupied by the entity.

Finally, the 42 Edgefield Road map will get overhauled later this year.

items.title: "Developers need to treat Early Access like a real launch, because players do" – Early Access games are on the rise, but so are player expectations
items.summary: The studios behind Valheim, Subnautica, Hades, Phasmophobia, Paralives, and Deadhaus Sonata discuss the highs and lows of Early Access
items.content:
The studios behind Valheim, Subnautica, Hades, Phasmophobia, Paralives, and Deadhaus Sonata discuss the highs and lows of Early Access

Image credit: GamesIndustry.biz Feature by Vic Hood Contributor Published on Oct. 27, 2026, 1:30 p.m. The number of games released through Steam's Early Access program has risen significantly in recent years. According to SteamDB , 2,924 Early Access games launched on Valve's platform in 2026 (as of mid-October), an 18% increase from 2025 and a 60% increase from 2020.

As a percentage of the overall number of Steam games released each year, Early Access titles are on the rise, going from a 10.4% share in 2024 to 11.3% in 2025 and 13.7% in 2026.

When Steam launched its Early Access program in 2013, it opened a valuable door for solo developers and smaller studios, allowing them to raise capital mid-development while simultaneously building hype and gathering vital player feedback ahead of a 1.0 launch. Don't Starve, Baldur's Gate 3, and Dead Cells are just some examples of how a constructive Early Access period can lead to long-term success.

But rather than simply buying time to tinker, a game's Early Access launch is now just as important as its "real" launch. GameDiscoverCo reported that only 21% of Steam Early Access graduates earned more in their first 30 days after 1.0 than after their Early Access release.

GamesIndustry.biz spoke to the studios behind Valheim, Subnautica, Hades, Phasmophobia, Paralives, and Deadhaus Sonata about the rising bar for Early Access releases, the benefits and pitfalls of gathering player feedback, and the things they would have done differently.

Nowadays, when it comes to Early Access, absolutely anything goes, says Anthony Gallegos, creative director of Subnautica 2. "It's not a few edge-case games participating anymore," he tells GamesIndustry.biz . "Early access could mean a game like ours doing long-term open development, or it could be a game three months from a 1.0 release that's effectively doing a paid beta soft launch and using the Early Access term as a way to soften player expectations."

All in all, that makes for a "more diverse and confusing landscape," he says.

One thing is certain though: competition in the Early Access space is higher than ever. Daniel Knight, CEO and game director at Phasmophobia maker Kinetic Games, says that whether Early Access or 1.0, new releases need to be at "a much higher quality." Paralives developer Alex Massé says he ended up delaying the game's Early Access launch from December 2025 to May 2026 after pre-release tests revealed the tutorials and some other features weren't up to scratch.

Richard Svensson, CEO of Valheim developer Iron Gate, believes that player expectations for an Early Access game are about 20% lower than for a full release, but they are still high. "They might be more forgiving when it comes to content, but they still expect a polished game."

However, for Denis Dyack, CEO of Deadhaus Sonata developer Apocalypse Studios, a key factor that's making the landscape more challenging is that anyone, including "giant publishers with insane amounts of money, manpower, and resources," can launch a game into Early Access.

"They can put up a polished product and rake in cash; it's a marketing beat for them," he explains. "So, that leaves players often expecting a near-perfect game that, in our opinion, defeats the purpose of Early Access, which is a collaborative development process based on player feedback. AAA publishers are abusing Early Access, skewing player expectations in such a way that it heavily disadvantages smaller independent developers." He cites Subnautica 2 and Path of Exile as examples of Early Access games "drastically changing the landscape and players' expectations."

Dyack explains that Apocalypse Studios never expected Deadhaus Sonata to be compared to Early Access games with AAA budgets and, as a result, says the team hit "significant barriers to entry" and had their marketplace impact "significantly reduced."

"Players naturally compare everything in the same marketplace, so smaller teams are being held to a much higher standard than they were in the past," adds Ethan McKinnon, creative director at Apocalypse Studios.

Phasmophobia Teams Up Again With American Heart Association for Fundraiser
items.summary: Phasmophobia keeps its finger on the pulse with its latest collaboration.
items.content:
Add DualShockers on Google Add as Preferred Source By Stephanie Watel Published Oct 26, 2026, 2:29 PM EDT Stephanie Watel is a Contributing Writer at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2022. She specializes in guides and reviews, with additional experience writing lists and features across RPGs, horror games, cozy sims, action games, open-world RPGs, JRPGs, and indie titles.

Before joining DualShockers, Stephanie contributed to GameRant , IGN , MovieWeb , Pro Game Guides , Twinfinite , and Prima Games . Her work has covered major releases, underground sleeper hits, and indie games across a wide range of genres. Stephanie holds a B.A. in English , including studies in journalism.

Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Since making a name for itself in the still-somewhat-niche online horror multiplayer space, Kinetic Games' Phasmophobia has gotten comfortable with doing occasional collaborations.

Whether it's for special limited-time merchandise launches or events like the Galaxies Gaming Showcase, Phasmophobia has been doing its part to keep things interesting as it continues working towards its multi-platform 1.0 launch next year .

However, there's one collab in particular that probably matters more than all the others combined, and it's starting today.

Whether you're exorcising ghosts or exploring tombs, there are many games that have similarities to Phasmophobia's co-op horror gameplay.

After its incredible success last year, Kinetic Games' Phasmophobia is teaming up once again with the American Heart Association Live for another Ghost Hunts for Hearts collaboration fundraiser, which goes directly to the American Heart Association and its many life-saving initiatives. The announcement was made via Kinetic Games' official website here .

To help bring this fundraiser directly to the players, official Kinetic Games Partners will be livestreaming their Phasmophobia gameplay via Twitch. The AHA collaboration event starts today, October 26, and will last exactly one week until November 2, 2026 . What's more, there's an in-game reward incentive for watching a certain amount of this livestream content.

If you watch at least 2 hours of Phasmophobia livestreams from a Kinetic Games Partner , you will get a special character ID Card and Badge for your in-game profile. The card itself displays a vibrant red aesthetic, decorated with a red blood cell background while the badge itself is a heart set aflame. Meanwhile, the title at the top is ' AHA Advocate ', which is certainly worthy one to display.

If you want to add this ID Card/Badge to your collection, make sure that your Phasmophobia profile is connected to your Twitch account, and you can check your status in-game via the Twitch link at the bottom of the lobby board. This will ensure that Twitch Drops are active for your profile. Once you reach the 2-hour mark of watching those livestreams, you should be able to redeem the ID Card reward in your inventory menu.

To make things even more exciting, Kinetic Games has mentioned that if the fundraiser surpasses their "secret fundraising goal", then an animated foil version of the AHA Advocate ID Card/Badge will be distributed to all players in-game. Back in the summer season of 2025, Phasmophobia's player community helped raise over $100,000 during the last Ghost Hunts for Hearts fundraiser stream event.

Since Phasmophobia has branched out to console platforms, its collaborative reach has continued to expand as well. Alongside its traditional seasonal in-game events that happen around every Easter, Halloween, and Christmas, the game's cult status has fostered some truly special collabs with various merch companies and organizations like the AHA.

Back in April of this year, Kinetic Games participated in the Galaxies Gaming Showcase, which featured the Astronomer ID Card Twitch Drop for players to collect. Soon after that, Phasmophobia collaborated with the beloved Alan Wake franchise on a weeks-long in-game event that coincided with the debut of the game's long-awaited character customization system . In October of last year, the game held a Twitch Drop collab during the annual TwitchCon event.

The AHA collaboration event starts today, October 26, and will last exactly one week until November 2, 2026. What's more, there's an in-game reward incentive for watching a certain amount of this livestream content.

Ghost Hunts For Hearts Returns
items.summary: Welcome back, Ghost Hunters. Today we’re excited to announce the return of Ghost Hunts for Hearts in collaboration with our good friends at American Heart Association Liive. Last year, the Phasmophobia community raised over $100,000 for the
items.content:
Welcome back, Ghost Hunters. Today we’re excited to announce the return of Ghost Hunts for Hearts in collaboration with our good friends at American Heart Association Liive.

Last year, the Phasmophobia community raised over $100,000 for the Heart Association's amazing cause and we’re hoping to go bigger and better this year by inviting the entire Phasmophobia community to join us.

We’re excited to share that we’re introducing a Twitch Drop as part of the campaign. From the get-go, any participating fundraising streamer will be able to distribute the event-exclusive Advocate ID Card & Badge throughout the week via any Phasmophobia stream.

We’re inviting any streamer that would like to take part in Ghost Hunts for Hearts via this link. Once registered, the Heart Liive team will be in contact to make sure you have everything you need to host your streams during the week of October 26th - November 2nd.

As an added bonus, if we reach our secret fundraising goal (which will be unveiled on the 26th), we’ll unlock the Animated version of this set for all players. Stay tuned for more details on the Drop as we get closer to event week!

You can find out more about American Heart Association Liive and the work they do by joining their Discord here.

We’re looking forward to seeing plenty of Ghost Hunts for Hearts at the end of the month!

Phasmophobia has sold more than 30 million copies across PC and console since entering Early Access in 2020. Developer Kinetic Games announced the milestone on October 8, alongside the return of its annual Crimson Eye Halloween event, which runs until November 1.

That number is absurd for a game that is still technically unfinished. CEO Daniel Knight started Phasmophobia alone at his parents' house. "My initial goal was to sell 1000 units in the first year," he said. "It's hard to believe we're celebrating 30 million".

Crimson Eye brings blood moon weather to a rotating set of maps each day. Ghosts move 15% faster, sanity drains twice as quickly, and events occur more frequently, but payouts are higher. The event maps are Tanglewood Drive, Camp Woodwind, Grafton Farmhouse, Bleasdale Farmhouse, Point Hope, Edgefield Road, Nell's Diner, and Willow Street.

Community goals unlock the Beholder ID Card and Badge, plus the Blood Moon Trophy. Personal goals unlock the Blood Moon Charm, a seasonal T-shirt, and upgrades to the Crimson Eye trophy. Twitch drops run through October 15, double XP runs from October 15 to 22, and Ghost Hunts 4 Hearts returns for the final week to support the American Heart Association. Last year's charity effort raised over $100,000.

The 1.0 release is now slated for the second half of 2027. Kinetic Games delayed it from 2026 to prioritize quality over speed, following a rocky reception to the Player Character Update. The studio apologized for that update, admitting it "missed the mark" and "didn't deliver on our promises". Sneak peeks of 1.0 development, including overhauls to ghost design and gameplay, will start next year. Phasmophobia is available on Steam, PS5, PS VR2, and Xbox Series X/S, with a Switch 2 version confirmed but undated.

Not everyone is celebrating. Steam community threads for the event are filled with frustration. One user wrote, "Seasonal events replaced with grindfests and lazy reskins." Another said, "Yawn, another boring event with a boring set of rewards." A third added, "It's like the devs didn't listen to the players when we said we hated this seasonal grindfest". The sentiment is not unanimous, but it is loud. The official Phasmophobia X account celebrated the milestone, noting the team is now 48 people and growing. That growth adds to the tension. A solo project that became a global phenomenon now has to satisfy a player base with wildly different expectations.

Kinetic Games also launched a publishing arm, Kinetic Publishing, earlier this year. Its first game, Contact Protocol , is due in Spring 2027. Whether that expansion helps or hurts the game that made it all possible is an open question. For now, 30 million sales and a Halloween event are a pretty good answer.

items.title: “Crimson Eye” Event Returns to ‘Phasmophobia’, Now Stands at 30 Million Sold
PHASMOPHOBIA LAUNCHES SEASONAL CRIMSON EYE EVENT AS GAME HITS 30 MILLION SALES
items.summary: It’s all treats and no tricks as the genre-defining co-op horror title hits a major milestone alongside the return of its annual Halloween eventSOUTHAMPTON,...
items.content:
Press release — 8 October 2026 12:27 Share Share this story Copy link Link copied! Download

It’s all treats and no tricks as the genre-defining co-op horror title hits a major milestone alongside the return of its annual Halloween event

SOUTHAMPTON, UK – October 8th, 2026 – Today, Kinetic Games announces that Phasmophobia has surpassed 30 million sales since its Early Access release across PC and console as its annual in-game Halloween event, Crimson Eye, launches for another year of terrifying hunts and seasonal rewards.

Since launching into Early Access in 2020, Phasmophobia has grown from a solo project into a global horror phenomenon, with Kinetic Games continuing to expand and evolve the game with new content and seasonal events. Until November 1st, Crimson Eye brings ghost hunters spectral rewards, spooktacular frights and bone-chilling challenges, with rotating event maps featuring blood moon weather for even more terrifying hunts. Ghosts have increased speed and sanity drains quicker, but brave players can earn higher rewards in return.

The fan-favourite fright has now been running for three years, with the blood moon first appearing in Phasmophobia in 2024. Crimson Eye returns this year as the team celebrates another major milestone: 30 million sales worldwide.

Starting as a solo project, Phasmophobia has grown into a global co-op horror phenomenon across PC and console. Throughout the game’s journey in Early Access, the Kinetic Games team has worked to expand haunted locations, introduce new ghost types and improve player character models, all shaped closely by community feedback.

This year alone, two major Quality of Life updates brought vast improvements to player characters, customisation and evidence collection, while introducing further Restricted maps for fast-paced ghost-hunting.

“So much has changed since I started making Phasmophobia on my own at my parents' house,” commented Daniel Knight, CEO of Kinetic Games and Game Director for Phasmophobia. “My initial goal was to sell 1000 units in the first year, so it’s hard to believe we’re celebrating 30 million. I’m so grateful to everyone who has played, and to the team who have worked alongside me on it. There is plenty more to come as we head towards 1.0.”

Phasmophobia’s success has also enabled Kinetic Games to expand its ambitions beyond the game itself, with the studio launching Kinetic Publishing earlier this year to champion independent development teams. Drawing on Daniel Knight’s journey from solo developer to global success, the publishing division gives indie devs the support and resources to make incredible games without compromising their creative vision. The first Kinetic Publishing Showcase in August revealed its first slate of titles, with its first game, starship job simulator Contact Protocol , launching in Spring 2027.

Looking ahead, the Kinetic Games team is gearing up for Phasmophobia’s highly anticipated 1.0 release, slated for the second half of 2027. Beginning next year, the studio will share spooky sneak peeks into the update’s development, including major overhauls to ghost design and overall gameplay.

The Crimson Eye event is available now in Phasmophobia, including:

Ghost Hunts 4 Hearts with the American Heart Association

Phasmophobia is available in Early Access on Steam , PS5 , PS VR2 , and Xbox Series X|S , priced at $19.99/£16.75/€19.50.

Assets for this announcement can be found here . For more information on the Crimson Eye event, please see the blog post here .

items.content:
Welcome back, Ghost Hunters. We have an update for you.

Today’s small update is in preparation for Crimson Eye, launching 8th October 2026, with the focus on getting the game ready for the start of the event. Our next major update, our move to Unity 6 is scheduled for November and will feature a host of bug fixes and improvements, all of which we’ll detail in an upcoming Development Preview.

New

 

  • Crimson Eye - The Crimson Eye is upon us, Ghost Hunters. Once more, various locations across Phasmophobia will be bathed in the red glow of the Blood Moon, offering any willing Ghost Hunter rewards in return for completing investigations, optional objectives and more. For more information on this year’s iteration of the event, please read our latest blogpost. 

    [/*]

  • Seasonal Event toggle - As a new feature for Crimson Eye and future seasonal events, we have implemented a toggle that allows players to turn on/off the event maps for their session. 

    [/*]

 

Fixes

  • Fixed an issue that caused the white light upon being revived to flash rather than slowly fade in and out.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where an Easter Egg reward may not unlock, despite a 0x multiplier being active and the reward pop up being displayed.

    [/*]

Known Issues

  • The lampposts outside of 6 Tanglewood Drive may glow when viewed by the player.

    [/*]

  • The Fusebox location will not be hidden on the Truck map when playing on a custom difficulty.

items.title: Phasmophobia Update 1.000.049 Released on October 7 to Prep for Crimson Eye
items.summary: Phasmophobia update 1.000.049 is live on consoles and PC, and this brings the Crimson Eye data for the event start tomorrow.
items.content:
It’s another October, and this means another Halloween-themed event is headed to Phasmophobia players. While this year’s Crimson Eye event won’t start until tomorrow, October 8, Kinetic Games has pushed out Phasmophobia update 1.000.049 to pre the game for it.

The event will run from October 8 to November 1, which gives plently of time for multiplayer horror fans to partake in the ghoulish festivities.

For the event details and changes made, read on for the official patch notes straight from Kinetic Games

As with previous years’ events, the Crimson Eye will cast its presence across several locations in Phasmophobia. Playing on these locations will grant each player event points, working towards unlocking the Community and Personal rewards, details of which are below.

The following list of locations will be featured throughout the event:

For those of you who have taken part in previous Crimson Eye events, you’ll know what to expect, but you’ll also get to see how Nell’s Diner and the reworked 6 Tanglewood Drive & 13 Willow Street look dressed in red. For newer Ghost Hunters, you’ll be tasked with hunting down Blood Moon totems and completing investigations and optional objectives to earn points, all while under the threat of Blood Moon weather, increasing the challenge you’ll face from ghosts.

Players will have several different unlockable rewards during the event: a seasonal event tee, the Beholder ID Card & Badge set and the Blood Moon charm.

Alongside these will be the upgradeable trophy. If you have previously unlocked this, you’ll continue to earn points and upgrades to your existing Trophy, rather than a new one.

During the event, we have a few different plans in place, so please do read on to learn what’s in store throughout October.

items.content:
Once more, Ghost Hunters, we pay homage to the Blood Moon. Our dear Crimson Eye.

Today, we’re excited to reveal that this year’s Crimson Eye event will begin on October 8th, 2026, and run until November 1st, 2026. An update containing the event will be deployed on October 6th.

As with previous years’ events, the Crimson Eye will cast its presence across several locations in Phasmophobia. Playing on these locations will grant each player event points, working towards unlocking the Community and Personal rewards, details of which are below.

The following list of locations will be featured throughout the event:

  • 6 Tanglewood Drive

    [/*]

  • 42 Edgefield Road

    [/*]

  • Grafton Farmhouse

    [/*]

  • 13 Willow Street

    [/*]

  • Bleasdale Farmhouse

    [/*]

  • Point Hope (Standard only, Point Hope Restricted will not be included)

    [/*]

  • Camp Woodwind

    [/*]

  • Nell’s Diner

    [/*]

For those of you who have taken part in previous Crimson Eye events, you’ll know what to expect, but you’ll also get to see how Nell’s Diner and the reworked 6 Tanglewood Drive & 13 Willow Street look dressed in red. For newer Ghost Hunters, you’ll be tasked with hunting down Blood Moon totems and completing investigations and optional objectives to earn points, all while under the threat of Blood Moon weather, increasing the challenge you’ll face from ghosts.

Players will have several different unlockable rewards during the event: a seasonal event tee, the Beholder ID Card & Badge set and the Blood Moon charm.

Alongside these will be the upgradeable trophy. If you have previously unlocked this, you’ll continue to earn points and upgrades to your existing Trophy, rather than a new one.

During the event, we have a few different plans in place, so please do read on to learn what’s in store throughout October.

Twitch Drop

During the first week of Crimson Eye, a Twitch Drop campaign will be running for all Phasmophobia streamers. After watching a total of two hours of Phasmophobia streams, you’ll earn the Crimson Eye tee. The campaign will be live from the moment the event begins until 11:59 PM BST on October 15th, 2026.

Double XP & Rewards

As is becoming tradition with Phasmophobia’s seasonal events, we’ll be running a Double XP & Rewards event during Crimson Eye. This will be taking place between October 15th–22nd, with all rewards from completed investigations being doubled during this period. Mark your calendars, Ghost Hunters!

Ghost Hunts 4 Hearts with the American Heart Association

Finally, during the final week of Crimson Eye (October 26th–November 1st), we’ll be bringing back Ghost Hunts 4 Hearts with our friends over at the American Heart Association! Last year, the Phasmophobia community raised over $100,000, which was an incredible achievement and went a long way towards helping the AHA team with their important work.

This year, we’re planning to go bigger and better; this event, and its rewards, will be accessible to all Phasmophobia creators & players when it goes live. While we’ll share details nearer the time, we just wanted to get the dates in your calendars!

We look forward to celebrating our favourite season with you once again, Ghost Hunters.

items.title: The Steam Frame's First Halloween: 189 Certified Games, and None of Our Ten Scariest
items.summary: Valve rates Phasmophobia Unsupported on Steam Frame, on a build that no longer ships. Seven more of our ten scariest VR games have no rating at all. What is…
items.content:
I went looking for Phasmophobia first. October started this morning, my Steam Frame reservation is still sitting in Valve's queue with no purchase email attached to it, and the one useful thing I can do while I wait is plan what goes on the headset when it shows up. So I opened Valve's Great on Frame list, 189 certified games as of today , and searched for the one I would want on Halloween night with three friends and a bad idea.

Phasmophobia has a Steam Frame rating in its app record, and the rating is Unsupported. One test, dated July 22. One result line: UnsupportedGraphicsPerformance, the same token Valve hung on its own showcase, The Lab , a week later. On the Steam Deck the same game is rated Playable.

That sent me back to my ranking of the ten scariest VR games with the same lookup open in another tab. None of the ten is certified.

Two were never eligible. Resident Evil 7's VR mode only ever shipped on PlayStation VR, and Resident Evil 4 VR is a Quest game. Neither exists on Steam in a headset.

That leaves eight. Phasmophobia is the only one Valve has rated at all. The other seven are MADiSON VR , Alien: Rogue Incursion , Half-Life: Alyx , The Walking Dead: Saints & Sinners , Five Nights at Freddy's: Secret of the Mimic , Into the Radius 2 and Metro Awakening , and none of them carries a Steam Frame compatibility record in its app data. No rating of any kind.

A blank is not a failing grade. It means Valve has not published a verdict, and plenty of unrated games will run. It also only describes what plays on the headset itself. Anything streamed from a gaming PC over the Frame's wireless adapter sits outside the program entirely, so if you own that PC, all eight of these behave the way they do on any other PC VR headset and you can close this tab.

The people this matters to are the ones buying a Frame as their only machine. For them the badge is the shopping list. And the shopping list has a hole where the horror aisle should be.

One exception is hiding in the box. Half-Life: Alyx runs on the Frame with no PC in the room , a copy comes with every headset, and it still is not on the certified list. Which means the Jeff chapter, number four on my ranking and the reason I once tiptoed across my own living room, is on every Frame Valve ships. The scariest hour a PC-less owner gets on day one lives in a game Valve has not rated.

Little Nightmares VR: Altered Echoes is the real one. Its certification test is dated August 18, its app record points at Lepton, Valve's Android runtime, and it lists at $29.99, marked down to $19.49 when I looked this morning. In April I wrote that I would play it with the lights on. I did. They stayed on.

Then there is Ravenholm. Half-Life 2: VR Mod cleared certification in August , it costs nothing, and the town you were told in 2004 not to go to is in it. I have played that chapter in the mod. It works as horror for a reason nobody designing it twenty-two years ago could have planned: the gravity gun is the main weapon, so every kill begins with you pointing your own arm at a saw blade lying on the ground while something shuffles closer. Episode One is certified too. Episode Two is not on the list.

Getting it is the easy part. It installs from its Steam page like any other game. The catch is ownership: the mod is free, but it needs Half-Life 2 in your own Steam library, and a family-shared copy does not count. The team keeps setup notes on its own site .

Deadly Delivery is the multiplayer pick more or less by default. I have not played it, so this is the store page talking: up to six delivery goblins hauling parcels into haunted mines, online co-op, $9.99 at list, 90 percent positive. Horror is its second Steam tag, right behind VR, and Comedy is its third, so expect something closer to a scream-and-laugh than a scare. With Phasmophobia off the table it is the certified answer to what four of us play on the 31st.

Zombies are covered. Arizona Sunshine 2 and the Arizona Sunshine Remake are both certified, if shooting the undead in broad desert daylight counts as Halloween in your house.

The flatscreen half of the shelf, which is now 102 of the 189, arguably does better than the VR half. DREDGE is a fishing game that turns Lovecraftian once the sun goes down. INSIDE is Playdead being Playdead. Both are certified, and both play on a virtual screen inside the headset, which is not what anybody bought a VR headset for and is still a perfectly good way to spend a night in late October.

items.content:
Welcome back, Ghost Hunters. We’ve got an update for you.

Today, we have released an update for Phasmophobia to address several issues that were raised following our latest Quality of Life update. Thank you to everyone who has helped with information and feedback to help us identify and fix these bugs.

Our next update following this will be our transition to Unity 6. This will be releasing in November, which is just a little shift from our original aim of October. We’ll be talking in more detail about this update as well as our cosmetics update in an upcoming Development Preview. Rest assured, our Crimson Eye event is still scheduled for October. More on that at a later date too.

Full patch notes for today’s release can be found below:

New

    [/*]

items.content:
Welcome back, Ghost Hunters.

Today we have released Phasmophobia v0.19.0.0, our latest update that brings with it the second part of our Quality of Life update. Full patch notes can be found below, and in-depth details on what’s new can be found in this blog.

New

  • Added new Restricted variants of the below maps.

    [/*]

  • Prison

    • Brownstone High School

      [/*]

    • Point Hope

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Video Cameras, Photo Cameras and Sound Recorders will now indicate Duplicate evidence.

    [/*]

  • Tier 1 Photo Cameras will display a yellow LED light.

    • Tier 2 & 3 Photo Cameras and all Tiers of Video Cameras will display faded text rather than the usual bold white text.

      [/*]

    • Tier 1 Sound Recorder will lower the brightness of the Volume indicators.

      [/*]

    • Tier 2 & 3 Sound Recorders will display faded sound waves.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • The Journal will now display other player selections of Evidence and Ghost Type.

    [/*]

  • The Keys section in the Journal has been replaced with Items We’ve Found, this new section will show keys, the bone and seasonal event collectables.

    [/*]

  • Added the ability to select the Ghost Type in a Custom Difficulty which will set the multiplier to 0.

    [/*]

  • Added a new Legacy Badge section to the Customisation shop to allow you to edit your badge at any time.

    [/*]

  • Players without a Legacy Badge will not see this option.

    [/*]

  • Added a ‘Hold Use’ sticky note on the Training whiteboards.

    [/*]

  • Dead players and dead player bodies will now look dead.

    [/*]

  • Added unique video evidence text for shower and fuse box interactions.

    [/*]

  • Added an icon to show whether a ghost name is male or female.

    [/*]

  • The Evidence page will now highlight the required Ghost evidence when the player selects a Ghost type.

    [/*]

Changes

  • Photo and Video Camera screens will now disable when clipping through a wall

    [/*]

  • When speaking, the speaker icon on ID cards will now function for all players, including local player

    [/*]

  • Improvements have been made to the VR character rig, allowing for more accurate and responsive movement.

    [/*]

  • Players can now interact with a Spirit Box when not grabbed using Text Voice Recognition Mode

    [/*]

    [/*]

  • The Truck has been moved closer to the main entrance on Brownstone High School and Prison

General Fixes

    [/*]

    [/*]

    [/*]

    [/*]

Ghost Fixes

    [/*]

Environment Fixes

    [/*]

    [/*]

  • This issue led players to believe this was evidence of a Yurei.

    [/*]

    [/*]
